correctness.rationale: Select a weak composition p0+⋯+pk=n−k and choices ci∈[0,pi], i<k. A constructive interleaving of two copies of X=0^p0 1 ⋯ 1 0^pk has gap vector (p0+c0,p0−c0,...,p_(k−1)+c_(k−1),p_(k−1)−c_(k−1),2pk). It is explicitly a shuffle square, and the gap vector uniquely recovers p,c. Thus the number of distinct outputs is ∑_compositions∏_(i<k)(pi+1)=[z^(n−k)](1−z)^(−(2k+1))=binom(n+k,2k); upper bound binom(2n,2k) counts all words with 2k ones. Both are Θ_k(n^(2k)) for fixed k; no assertion of leading constant for k>=2. Independently enumerated construction/inverse at small n,k; analytic injection is the infinite proof.
residual_risks: n≥k≥1 and fixed k in the asymptotic; when k grows with n the Θ_k statement is not uniform.
The exact n^(2k) exponent does not determine the leading coefficient for k≥2.
